response: No, not all ethnic groups in New Zealand exhibit socio-economic mortality gradients in the same way. While the general pattern of higher mortality rates among more disadvantaged socio-economic groups is observed in the overall New Zealand population, research suggests that this gradient is less pronounced or even reversed in some ethnic groups, particularly among Māori and Pacific populations. In these groups, the relationship between socio-economic status and mortality is more complex and may be influenced by cultural and social factors.
